question.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(5x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x=2\sqrt{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{2}⁡(5x)}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{2}⁡(5x))(2\sqrt{x})-\int (2\sqrt{x})(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\sqrt{x}{log}_{2}⁡(5x)-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{4\sqrt{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x)-2)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$
